message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the order **Carnivora** (sub‑order Feliformia), while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the order **Perissodactyla** (odd‑toed ungulates).  
Both orders are part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which also contains groups such as ungulates, bats, whales, and many other mammals.

Therefore, the most recent common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatherian clade.  
This ancestor would have been a small, probably insectivorous or omnivorous mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous to early Paleogene period, before the diversification of the major Laurasiatherian lineages.
